implementation_notes: Prisma makes the key explicit in the schema: the child model declares the scalar foreign key field and the relation field, tied by @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade), and the generated client returns typed objects where include/select decides whether the reference is resolved. TypeORM's decorator equivalent is @ManyToOne plus @JoinColumn (and @JoinTable for junction tables), with eager/lazy/cascade options on the relation. A hand-written mapper over a driver is justified only in deliberately thin data layers, since the schema-first client already carries the mapping.
pitfalls: The relation field and the foreign key field must agree on nullability; the schema checker rejects one-sided optionality, and omitting the scalar field hides the key from your own queries.
include is a per-query join: touching post.author in a loop without include/select is an N+1 that TypeScript cannot warn about because the field is simply deferred.
Database-level cascade deletes bypass application hooks, so audit or event logic attached to the ORM never runs for cascaded children.
